description: issue #682 (slice I3): a `when "stop" [ ... ]` handler is DEFERRED at registration — unlike `"start"`, the standard `"stop"` event (a requested stop notification before termination, spec/interaction-events.md's `### when <event-word> <block>` and "Time, ticks, and handlers") is not being delivered yet, so registering it emits only the `instruction`+`primitive` pair (seq 0-1) and does NOT run the block. The following `print "mid"` runs normally (seq 2-3). The `"stop"` event is delivered once when the batch run reaches its end, before termination, so the deferred handler fires last (seq 4-6): its block-start `instruction` carries the `when` keyword's span (seq 4), then `print "bye"` runs (seq 5-6). This proves registration is not invocation and that a deferred handler fires exactly once at the deterministic stop moment.
